title.zh: 轴对称多矩形线圈真空场

summary: Expand rectangular coil records into weighted filaments, evaluate each coil response, and superpose the drive currents.

capability: Expand rectangular coil records into weighted filaments, evaluate each coil response and superpose the drive currents.
operation: rectangular-coil records and target grid -> vacuum fields and filament table
discovery.model: Ordered acyclic composition of rectangular geometry, circular Green response and current contraction.
discovery.geometry: Matching rectilinear target grid and nonempty ordered coil list.
discovery.boundary: Input validation or any dependency failure aborts the call without a fallback or partial field.

identity.direction: rectangular-coil records and target grid to vacuum fields and filament table
identity.definition: For each caller coil, discretize centers, attach weights, evaluate Green responses, contract one drive current, and reshape to the input grid.
identity.model: Ordered acyclic composition of rectangular geometry, circular Green response, and current contraction.
identity.geometry: Matching rectilinear target grid and nonempty ordered coil list.
identity.coordinates: Grid and coil geometry in metres; currents in amperes; output psi Wb/rad and fields tesla.
identity.boundary: Input validation or any dependency failure aborts the call without a fallback or partial field.
assumptions: Target grids are finite, matching, and strictly increasing in R and Z.
Each coil mapping has the required finite fields and optional weights/angle.
Returned filament rows preserve coil and within-coil order.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear 2-D grid; radial axis is strictly increasing and nonnegative.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.constraints: Finite, same shape as r_grid, and axial axis strictly increasing.

inputs.name: rectangular_coils
inputs.description: Coil mappings with r0_m,z0_m,nr,nz,dr_m,dz_m,current_a and optional angle_deg/weights.
inputs.constraints: Nonempty; one finite drive current and one optional finite weight per generated filament.

outputs.name: psi_vac
outputs.description: Vacuum poloidal flux on the target grid.
outputs.constraints: Same grid shape and C-order point mapping as inputs.

outputs.name: b_r_vac
outputs.description: Vacuum radial magnetic field on the target grid.
outputs.constraints: Same grid shape and C-order point mapping as inputs.

outputs.name: b_z_vac
outputs.description: Vacuum axial magnetic field on the target grid.
outputs.constraints: Same grid shape and C-order point mapping as inputs.

outputs.name: filaments
outputs.description: Concatenated [R_m,Z_m,weight] rows in caller coil order.
outputs.constraints: Preserves each coil's filament order and the outer caller coil order.

preconditions: Target grids are finite, matching, and strictly increasing in R and Z.
Each coil mapping has the required finite fields and optional weights/angle.
supported: One or more rectangular coils, optional weights/rotation, C-order reshaping, and dependency failure propagation.
excluded: Iterative coil solving, nonlinear materials, finite-wire effects, and malformed/empty coil lists.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for missing or malformed grids, empty/nonmapping coils, invalid geometry, weights, or currents.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Dependency ValueError/FloatingPointError propagates before any field is returned, including a nonrepresentable current-weighted Green contraction; no fallback or retry is performed.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the graph has no feedback loop.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No field or filament output is returned after a failed graph stage.

example.description: Expand one 2x2 rectangular coil on a 2x2 target grid and evaluate its vacuum field.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import solve_multi_coil_vacuum_field
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.2], [-0.1, 0.1])
result = solve_multi_coil_vacuum_field(r_grid=r_grid, z_grid=z_grid, rectangular_coils=[{'r0_m': 0.45, 'z0_m': 0.0, 'nr': 2, 'nz': 2, 'dr_m': 0.04, 'dz_m': 0.05, 'current_a': 1000.0}])
assert result['psi_vac'].shape == r_grid.shape
assert result['filaments'].shape == (4, 3)
assert np.isfinite(result['b_z_vac']).all()
example.expected: The three field arrays have shape (2,2), the returned filament table has shape (4,3), and b_z_vac is finite.

scope: Linear scaling with coil drive current.
Independent response rows for multiple coils.
Missing current and invalid grid failures.
Unrepresentable near-wire or high-current responses fail closed instead of returning nonfinite fields.

Fixed Pleiades two-coil reference values and, when the external truth artifact is present, the full 9x9 truth arrays are covered by tests/cross_domain/multi_coil_vacuum_field/test_pleiades_two_coil_truth.py.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Verified for the declared axisymmetric vacuum-filament model and tested input contracts; it does not establish applicability to material coils, plasma response, or three-dimensional geometry.
known_limitations: No field cache or device object is kept between calls.
No feedback, optimization, or conductor-material model is included.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

nodes.description: Iterate caller coil mappings and expose one validated parameter set in caller order.
Append dimensionless filament weights and preserve one coil drive current.
Pack matching rectilinear grids into C-order R-Z target rows.
Evaluate one Green response row for the current coil block.
Stack one completed response row and drive current per coil without multiplication.
Contract coil currents with the stacked response rows.
Concatenate weighted filament blocks only for the returned diagnostic table.

execution.ordering: Validate inputs, iterate coils in caller order, discretize and evaluate each response independently, stack completed rows, superpose once, and reshape outputs.
execution.state_ownership: Caller owns grid and coil declarations; the graph owns only local ordered lists for the current call and retains no mutable state.
execution.failure_propagation: Validation or dependency failure aborts the call immediately; no fallback, retry, or partial field result is produced.
